I find myself wondering about socialism in this context lately. I wonder about the Nazis, and how they turned the shithole Weimar Republic into the powerhouse of Europe in a decade or so, while running a version of socialism.

The question I come to is this - why don't the socialists get together and use their wealth for the benefit of each other? My family and I have helped each other out, through both effort and money, and it benefitted all of us without anyone becoming leeches or our house's economy collapsing. Why does this not work large scale, with the possible exception of Nazi Germany?

The common thread I see with my family and the Nazi ideology - we believed ourselves to function like one tribe, where we were all valuable to each other as part of the same in-group, and where everyone was expected and pushed to sacrifice for each other. Everyone had a role, and we put our own group first among all. We identified with each other. And not everyone was equal, nor was equality of outcome a goal. Some were more successful due to their own ability or effort or experience, and they were expected to live and lead in accordance with their own success, so long as it did not directly damage other members of the group or their freedom to do the same. Competition was celebrated along with cooperation.

We have no in-groups anymore. If you look at socialist nations, the nation is simply lines on a map, not a people. The elites and common people function as separate societies, and the common people have little reason to identify with each other. Sacrifice is not expected, and leeches are not only allowed, they are legally enshrined. Competition is pointless because everyone is offered a basically equal outcome regardless of effort. Cooperation is pointless because there is no celebrated in-group for whom all members are bettered by the success of any one member. There is no tribe.

I think this is what Hitler may have been trying to accomplish through his policies, whether anyone thinks they were good or not. The "ethnic purity" policies were building Germany as single people who identified with each other, not simply a land mass ruled by one government. The socialist work programs were building a nation where the basics of life could always be provided by sacrificing to the group, rather than by simply waiting for handouts. The business regulation was building industry that succeeded by being most beneficial to the tribe, rather than by whatever means might make money regardless of damage to, or paracitism of the whole. And there were plenty of unequal outcomes due to effort and ability, with no promise that it might be otherwise.

I don't know if his society would have worked in the long run. I don't know if it is a feasible situation in such a "multicultural" world. I certainly would not endorse genocide as a solution. But I wonder - if you gathered a group that viewed themselves as a single tribe who shared interests and culture, who were sharing a world narrative of mutual sacrifice and benefit, who followed a leader that was one of them and necessarily owed more of his own success to the benefit he brought to the tribe rather than to the special interests he pleased... could a socialist society work? I don't know, but there's precious little examples of this that weren't crushed by international interests, unlike the more common Marxist socialism which seems to just collapse under it's own weight.
